title: First saxophone jobs and falling asleep in Spanish class
summary: The market-opening band led to many jobs, taking over his father's engagements, until parents curbed his working because school suffered.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You were what age? You were in high school, what age?

I was in high school. I was about 14, 15 years old. I was about 15. So, I went out that Saturday and I played on the job and it went over. So, the next week, there was an opening of another market and the man called and asked for the same band that played for his opening of his market. So I went to another market out in Southgate, it was right close to Huntington Park, and I played at another opening of a market in Southgate.
The word sort of got around to the new saxaphone player in South --

-- so people started calling up. They already knew my dad. He was a saxaphone player and we had the same name. So then, when they called to the house for my dad for a job, if he already had one on that night, he says, 'Well, I can send my son out. He can play.' So, I started taking my dad's jobs

as his substitute.

So, that's how I started playing saxophone. So, inside of about a year, I had more jobs than I could take until my parents had to stop me from actually working because I was messing up my schooling, because I'd be falling asleep in my first class. I never did learn how to speak Spanish because my first class every morning was my Spanish class and I couldn't get my conjugation of the verbs together on my Spanish and to this day, I never accomplished the speaking of Spanish, although I took it for two years. I was always sleeping everytime the teacher called me.
So, that's when I started working regularly at night, at the time, about 15, only on weekends. But then my parents finally let me take a regular job at a taxi dance and when I was 16.
